measurement_class_legend.BEHAVIORALLY_PROVEN: A probe executed and the control's condition was met.
measurement_class_legend.BEHAVIORALLY_FAILED: A probe executed and the control's condition was NOT met.
measurement_class_legend.IMPLEMENTED_BUT_UNMEASURED: The capability demonstrably exists but no evaluator measures it, so the control defaults to BLOCKED. This is NOT a behavioural failure.
measurement_class_legend.ABSENT: The capability genuinely does not exist.
measurement_class_legend.NOT_EVALUABLE: A prerequisite (service, evidence artifact, configuration) is unavailable.
measurement_class_legend.EXTERNAL: Resolution is owned outside engineering and must never be self-approved.

verified_environment_with_evidence.note: NOT MEASURED: this checkout has no local evidence artifact, so this context is identical to the fresh-checkout context. Regenerate evidence to measure it.

controls.resolution_condition: Audit entry hashes are computed with a managed secret key (HMAC), so a state-file writer cannot forge a valid chain.
controls.implemented_capability: Versioned HMAC-SHA256 audit chain with key rotation and retained verification-only keys; the probe signs a fresh event and requires a public-SHA forgery to be rejected. Backed by an 86-check behavioural guard. Evaluates PASS whenever an active key is set.
controls.missing_capability: No code gap. The control reads BLOCKED only when the evaluated environment has no MONDAY_REPORT_AUDIT_HMAC_KEY. The resolution phrase 'a state-file writer cannot forge' additionally assumes key custody separate from the state file, which env-var injection on the same host does not by itself establish.
controls.notes: The GA client env generator previously omitted this key entirely, producing an environment in which every protected route failed closed. Fixed on this branch.

controls.resolution_condition: An externally persisted append-only anchor (event count + head hash) exists so deleting trailing events breaks integrity verification.
controls.implemented_capability: None. HMAC protects entry content, not entry existence.
controls.missing_capability: An external anchor in a second trust domain. audit_integrity_status derives total_events from len(events), so a truncated chain still verifies clean -- the project proves this deliberately in its own guard.
external_dependencies: external anchor service or immutable object-lock storage
controls.notes: docs/AUDIT_INTEGRITY.md explicitly rejects a same-process checkpoint as a substitute.

controls.resolution_condition: A backup mechanism and an evidenced, tested restore drill exist for the production persistence backend with defined RPO/RTO.
controls.implemented_capability: None. The only repository-wide match for pg_dump/RPO/RTO is the registry entry itself.
controls.missing_capability: A backup mechanism, an evidenced restore drill, and organizationally approved RPO/RTO.
controls.notes: Cannot reach PASS from documentation alone.

controls.resolution_condition: A CI workflow runs the build and audit:all (and the corpus-backed FORGE evaluation) on every push and blocks merges on failure.
controls.implemented_capability: None. No .github directory exists anywhere in the repository.
controls.missing_capability: A committed workflow AND an observed run for the exact commit with no required job skipped, bound to an immutable run identifier.
controls.notes: Committing YAML alone must not flip this control.

controls.implemented_capability: A demo-seed marker triggers a self-wipe to a clean workspace.

controls.resolution_condition: A verified, signed client/organizational approval is recorded through a supported mechanism with an authenticated approver identity.
controls.implemented_capability: None.

controls.resolution_condition: Correction lineage integrity is guaranteed across processes via normalized persistence with row/advisory locking or a uniqueness constraint.
controls.implemented_capability: Correction lineage is enforced only by an in-process lock. There is no field_corrections table at all.
controls.missing_capability: A normalized corrections table with row/advisory locking or a uniqueness constraint on the active lineage.
controls.notes: Resolution language quoted verbatim: 'Correction lineage integrity is guaranteed across processes via normalized persistence with row/advisory locking or a uniqueness constraint.' Unlike persistence-locking-transactions this explicitly requires NORMALIZED persistence, so a transactional snapshot cannot close it.

controls.resolution_condition: A migration runner with a schema_migrations/version table applies db/migrations/ deterministically and idempotently.
controls.implemented_capability: Deterministic runner with schema_migrations metadata, session advisory lock, per-migration transactions, checksum-drift refusal; proven on real PostgreSQL 16.14.
controls.missing_capability: None. PASS requires the local evidence artifact to be present.
controls.notes: Evidence artifact lives under output/ which is gitignored, so a fresh checkout correctly falls back to BLOCKED. That is fail-closed behaviour, not a regression.

controls.resolution_condition: All committed migrations reference only tables/columns created by earlier migrations; FK targets exist.
controls.implemented_capability: Corrected fresh-install baseline in db/baseline/ applies cleanly on real PostgreSQL.
controls.missing_capability: The immutable legacy sequence remains un-appliable: 0003 references projects(id) and reports(id), which no earlier legacy migration creates. Fails on real PostgreSQL at version 3 with 'relation "projects" does not exist'.
controls.notes: Deliberately BLOCKED. The historical migration is NOT rewritten because its never-deployed status cannot be proven. The probe independently re-runs the static validator over db/migrations/, so a passing baseline cannot flip it.

controls.resolution_condition: The official-export gate is verified by behavior: an unreviewed report cannot officially export, required review blocks it, and provenance is enforced.
controls.implemented_capability: Exports are blocked with HTTP 409 while any validation task is open.
controls.missing_capability: A provenance-enforcing gate. The evaluator explicitly refuses callable-method presence as evidence.

controls.resolution_condition: A fresh corpus-backed FORGE evaluation report exists with 65/65 required PASS and manifest/expectations SHA-256 matching the committed files.
controls.implemented_capability: A FORGE corpus evaluation harness exists with a manifest and expectations.
controls.missing_capability: A passing forge report must be supplied; the probe currently receives none.

controls.resolution_condition: Authenticated per-user credentials replace the single shared API key and the request actor is derived from the caller's identity.
controls.implemented_capability: Per-user identity is implemented: opaque high-entropy credentials, SHA-256 + optional pepper at-rest hashing with constant-time compare, non-secret fingerprints, active/revoked credential status, per-user records with roles and account_status, admin-gated HTTP provisioning, an offline provisioning CLI, request-scoped identity in a ContextVar, and audit actor fields derived from the resolved caller. Client mode explicitly REJECTS the legacy shared key for authentication.
controls.missing_capability: No behavioural evaluator exists, so the control defaults to BLOCKED. Closing it honestly requires an evidence-driven probe plus a behavioural guard exercising real routes, and removal of the assertion that currently pins it BLOCKED.
controls.notes: The registry DESCRIPTION for this control is stale -- it predates the authenticated identity work. The RESOLUTION CONDITION is not stale and is not modified.

controls.resolution_condition: Multi-entity mutations run under a transaction/lock; no cross-process whole-snapshot last-writer-wins.
controls.implemented_capability: Nothing for application mutations. The universal pattern is refresh() -> mutate in memory -> save() rewriting the entire payload. The local store's tmp-file + replace is atomic FILE replacement only; it prevents torn files, not lost updates. PostgresStateStore.save() is a single-statement whole-payload upsert whose preceding read uses a separate connection and therefore a separate transaction.
controls.missing_capability: No SELECT FOR UPDATE, no advisory lock, no revision/CAS column, no conflict retry, no idempotency key. The only advisory lock in the repository belongs to the migration runner, which this control explicitly excludes. Three in-process RLocks concede last-writer-wins across processes in their own comments.
controls.notes: Resolution language quoted verbatim: 'Multi-entity mutations run under a transaction/lock; no cross-process whole-snapshot last-writer-wins.' It does NOT mandate normalized tables, so a transactional snapshot with row locking and revision compare-and-swap can satisfy it.

controls.resolution_condition: A local-AI extraction router exists with output validation, provenance, timeout/isolation, disabled-by-default posture, and no silent override of deterministic values.
controls.implemented_capability: Archive entry/size limits and sanitized tenant-scoped storage paths.
controls.missing_capability: A complete extraction trust boundary including parser crash isolation and export formula-injection neutralisation.

controls.resolution_condition: The requested repository backend is postgres, the active adapter is postgres via a live probe, and a database URL is configured.
controls.implemented_capability: A functional PostgresStateStore exists with RLS enabled/forced on the snapshot table and a tenant_slug GUC policy.
controls.missing_capability: Requires a reachable PostgreSQL configured as the ACTIVE adapter to evaluate at all. Two latent defects: readiness reads boot-time store attributes, so the 'live probe' is live only at process construction; and the Postgres SQL path has no test coverage -- no guard ever instantiates PostgresStateStore against a database.

controls.resolution_condition: Client mode is enabled and every configuration readiness check (API key >=24, signing secret >=32, out-of-repo state/storage/export paths, upload/archive/retention limits, hosted fallback disabled) passes.
controls.implemented_capability: A fail-closed client-data readiness module with roughly 25 checks already exists and is reusable.
controls.missing_capability: Delegated readiness ids are absent from the supplied map in a bare evaluation, so the control cannot evaluate.

controls.resolution_condition: Distinct roles with enforced least privilege exist and route authorization checks a per-user role, not the single configured all-role user.
controls.implemented_capability: Route-level RBAC with complete route coverage, proven by probe.
controls.missing_capability: None.

controls.resolution_condition: The requested queue backend is redis, the active worker is redis via a live probe, and a Redis URL is configured.
controls.implemented_capability: A Redis queue backend exists as an advisory filter over the snapshot.
controls.missing_capability: Requires a reachable Redis to evaluate. No ack, visibility timeout, retry or DLQ semantics, so it does not mitigate the lost-update problem.

controls.resolution_condition: All three fixture-evidence readiness checks pass: parser fixture evals, golden fixture coverage, and a reviewed anonymized-client attestation.
controls.implemented_capability: Golden-fixture and parser-eval readiness checks exist.
controls.missing_capability: A reviewed anonymized-client fixture manifest with an authenticated reviewer attestation.

controls.resolution_condition: Request/worker actions emit structured, redacted, correlation-id-bearing logs.
controls.implemented_capability: None.
controls.missing_capability: Structured logs with safe correlation fields across API, worker, persistence and security paths.

controls.resolution_condition: Tenant is resolved from the authenticated request and enforced at the API layer (with Postgres RLS active for the normalized store).
controls.implemented_capability: API-layer per-request tenant ownership is enforced and proven: every resource-scoped route carries a tenant-ownership dependency, the ownership graph fails closed on a contradictory chain, cross-tenant access is an existence-hiding 404, and list aggregates are tenant-filtered before counting.
controls.missing_capability: The resolution condition also requires Postgres RLS active over the normalized store. The Postgres adapter stores one JSONB snapshot per tenant_slug, and the normalized migration leaves every tenant_isolation policy commented out.
controls.notes: Route-level enforcement alone is explicitly insufficient for this condition.

controls.resolution_condition: Correction/validation outcomes attribute a verified authenticated human, not the configured actor context.
controls.implemented_capability: Terminal validation outcomes attribute a verified authenticated human.
controls.missing_capability: None.

controls.resolution_condition: The worker emits a liveness heartbeat and applies a documented retry/dead-letter policy; a stuck worker is detectable.
controls.implemented_capability: None. worker.py is a minimal run-once entry point.
controls.missing_capability: Persisted heartbeats, worker identity, stale detection, and honest unhealthy reporting when dependencies are down.
